observation_kind: Supplementary physical observations from this same review; not a separate blind identity review.

evidence: Native crops show paving between planted islands and damaged buildings, with dense structural fragments crossing the fixed line. At the central destruction and building frontage neither continuous opposite main-road margin can be recovered; the null polygon, empty objects and indeterminate scope are justified.

The fixed curved road is recognizable, but overlapping crowns conceal its western margins near B and the eastern terminal near A. Deep shadows alone are not entities. The full-width boundary and concealed surface cannot be checked, supporting indeterminate with no invented polygon or objects.

The southern planted-island edge is visible, but paving on the opposite side merges into the building frontage and damaged material. Native views confirm loose structural pieces without establishing a unique continuous complete main-road width; the indeterminate row and empty object list remain justified.

Three native views cover both terminal cross-sections and the full bend. Grass edges establish continuous main-road width across driveway openings. Both first-row small debris polygons match separate light raised pieces on the northeastern pavement, confirmed in the object crop; the target polygon preserves the A/B extent and excludes the adjoining frontage wreckage.

Native views confirm A sits in the arterial carriageway before the entrance, while the remainder follows the narrow access carriageway beside the planted divider. The complete main-road cross-section across that junction cannot be uniquely continued from the visible access-road width without choosing new terminal boundaries. Scattered edge fragments do not repair that missing definition; indeterminate is appropriate.

Four native crops cover A, B, both margins and the full diagonal. The continuous grass margins allow the driveway widths to be bridged without taking all frontage. The central collapsed panel/frame group intrudes onto paving; farther southwest the corrugated sheet, long strip and bent tube group match all four supplied debris polygons. The full-length road polygon and obstacle verdict are supported.

Native crops show the curving access pavement with small loose pieces and a substantial debris group on its eastern margin. A is on the intersecting arterial beyond the entrance mouth. The access-road margins cannot define a unique complete cross-section there; retaining the fixed scope makes the null target and indeterminate verdict justified.

Four native crops cover the entire building-side route and both endpoints. The southeast side has marked parking bays, interrupted curb/verge portions and long groups of loose frames and panels. No continuous main-road-versus-parking margin can be recovered through all these transitions from adjacent road width alone. Ordinary parked vehicles do not by themselves establish obstruction. The first-row unresolved boundary and indeterminate verdict remain justified.

The road and loose material are visible toward B, but A lies in the black unavailable wedge beyond the oblique image boundary; its terminal cross-section cannot be observed. This directly supports the missing-imagery uncertainty, null polygon and indeterminate full-scope assessment. No additional crop can reveal that absent terminal. Visible portions do not establish the presence or identity of the complete frozen target; unavailable portions remain unknown.

The visible access pavement leads from the arterial through trees and parking. B and the upper terminal portion are inside the large black image gap. Canopy also overlaps the visible approach. A complete fixed-scope boundary cannot be supplied, so the first-row indeterminate assessment is supported. Visible portions do not establish the presence or identity of the complete frozen target; unavailable portions remain unknown.

Visible pavement runs eastward from A, then the oblique image boundary removes the eastern terminal and B. This is unavailable imagery rather than a shadow. The fixed full-width target cannot be completed, supporting the null polygon, empty objects and indeterminate verdict. Visible portions do not establish the presence or identity of the complete frozen target; unavailable portions remain unknown.

The native-sized image shows an intermittent narrow paved route left of the fixed line amid overlapping crowns. Its full margins are not recoverable, while A is beyond the bottom image extent. Neither the terminal cross-section nor the concealed alignment can be established, so the existing indeterminate row is supported. Visible portions do not establish the presence or identity of the complete frozen target; unavailable portions remain unknown.

The visible portion contains an entrance and wide connected paving with scattered loose material. The final bend toward B exits through the oblique boundary into black unavailable imagery, including the entire B cross-section. This independently confirms the stated missing terminal; no complete target polygon or full-segment entity verdict is supportable. Visible portions do not establish the presence or identity of the complete frozen target; unavailable portions remain unknown.

The northeastern arterial lanes and outer margins are visible, but the southwest route and A fall in the large black image gap. The complete A/B scope cannot be identified from imagery alone. The first-row indeterminate verdict and missing southwestern cross-section uncertainty are justified. Visible portions do not establish the presence or identity of the complete frozen target; unavailable portions remain unknown.

Most of the vertical fixed scope, including A, lies in black unavailable imagery. Near B, dense overlapping crowns and structural wreckage conceal the surface and margins; imagery does not establish a physical continuous road there. Retaining indeterminate with null polygon and no asserted object membership is supported. Visible portions do not establish the presence or identity of the complete frozen target; unavailable portions remain unknown.

Paving is visible only near B beside the building. The image ends on an oblique boundary immediately northeast of that area, removing most of the fixed line and A. The missing A terminal prevents a complete full-width assessment; the original indeterminate row is justified. Visible portions do not establish the presence or identity of the complete frozen target; unavailable portions remain unknown.
